question: As a country develops, it undergoes ‘structural changes'. Which of the following is a indicator of these structural changes?

options.text: The share of the industrial sector in GDP decreases
The share of agriculture in GDP declines
The share of agriculture in GDP increases
The share of agriculture in GDP becomes more than 50 percent

solution:
The correct answer is __**The share of agriculture in GDP declines.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• Structural changes refer to the shift in the composition of an economy from one sector to another.
 
• The decline in the share of agriculture in **GDP is a common indicator of structural changes in a developing country.**
 
• This decline is usually accompanied by an increase in the share of the industrial and service sectors.
 
• Option 1 is incorrect as it suggests a decrease in the share of the industrial sector, which is not a typical indicator of structural changes.
 
• Option 4 is not a plausible scenario as it would mean that the country is heavily dependent on agriculture and has not diversified its economy.
 
• Option 3 is also incorrect as it contradicts the notion of structural changes and suggests that the country is moving towards a more agrarian economy.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is option 2, which indicates that the country is undergoing structural changes as it shifts away from agriculture toward other sectors.
